notes: Sources: Lake Shore FWPX technical-specifications page (cache research/v5/cache/9ae700052f15978d.txt) and Lake Shore Probe Stations catalog PDF probestationcatalog_l.pdf pp. 38-39 (cache research/v5/cache/75efd8eb8da79422.txt), whose cross-section diagram labels 'Radiation shield stage (20 K) / Sample stage (4.5 K) / Probe (25 K) / Probe arm base / Probe arm shield / Thermal anchors / Vacuum chamber base'. Scene geometry: a 406 mm OD x 178 mm tall nickel-plated aluminium vacuum chamber (330 mm top opening, 102 mm fused-quartz top viewport with 91 mm viewing area, NW40 pump port with isolation valve, NW25 gauge port, 0.25 in NPT gas port, 3.5 kPa relief valve) on a 1067 x 851 mm platform; inside, a nickel-plated aluminium radiation shield with 180 mm lid and 159 mm IR-absorbing window (152 mm viewing area) surrounds the 4.5 K x-y translating sample stage carrying a 102 mm grounded SH-4.00-G sample holder; six micromanipulated probe arms enter from the sides, arm anchored to the 20 K shield, probe anchored to the sample stage. Cooling is a 2-stage continuous-flow cryostat (sample + radiation shield) fed by a large-bore S-style LHe/LN2 transfer line with 12.7 mm top-port Dewar withdrawal; no compressor or cold head, so the only mechanical motion is cryogen flow, the pump, and operator-driven stage/probe moves. Base 4.5 K with up to 6 arms (3.5 K with PS-LT, not fitted); control range 5-475 K on the current web page (4.5-420 K in the catalog PDF); cooldown 1.5 h, warmup 1.5 h, cycle 3.5 h, vibration <30 nm, base pressure <1e-5 Torr, no magnet option, no backside optical access. The 'lhe_flow' enum covers both cryogens: the same flow circuit runs on LN2 (80 K) or LHe (5 K).
